title: Modi Dedicates Nitish Setu, New Six-Lane Ganga Bridge in Bihar
excerpt: The 19.7 km Kachhi Dargah–Bidupur crossing links Patna and Vaishali districts and anchors a ₹34,470 crore package of Bihar projects inaugurated on Saturday.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi dedicated Nitish Setu, a six-lane extradosed cable-stayed bridge over the Ganga in Bihar, to the nation on Saturday, November 21, 2026.
  • The 19.7 km project — a 9.7 km main bridge plus 10 km of approach roads — was built at a cost of around ₹4,280 crore and connects Kachhi Dargah in Patna district with Bidupur in Vaishali district.
  • The bridge gives north and south Bihar a new Ganga crossing and is expected to ease pressure on the Mahatma Gandhi Setu and the JP Setu; reported travel time between Patna and Vaishali via the bridge is 20 to 25 minutes.
  • The dedication was part of a wider ₹34,470 crore package of projects Modi inaugurated or laid foundation stones for in Vaishali, alongside a Griha Pravesh for over 26,900 PMAY (Urban) beneficiaries.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday dedicated Nitish Setu, a six-lane cable-stayed bridge across the Ganga, to the nation during a visit to Bihar's Vaishali district. Modi visited the bridge at around 1:15 p.m. before inaugurating and laying foundation stones for development projects worth around ₹34,470 crore at a public event in Vaishali, according to the Press Information Bureau. The bridge is named after former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar.

The bridge itself

Nitish Setu is an extradosed cable-stayed bridge built at a cost of around ₹4,280 crore. The 19.7 km project comprises a 9.7 km main bridge and 10 km of approach roads, connecting Kachhi Dargah on National Highway 22 in Patna district with Bidupur on National Highway 322 in Vaishali district, via Raghopur Diara. The Daily Jagran reported that the bridge was jointly constructed by Larsen & Toubro and South Korea's Daewoo Engineering and Construction under the supervision of the Bihar State Road Development Corporation, and that the crossing cuts the Patna–Vaishali journey to 20 to 25 minutes.

"Nitish Setu is an extradosed cable-stayed bridge built at a cost of around ₹4,280 crore."

Why it matters for Bihar

The Ganga splits Bihar, and its road crossings have long been bottlenecks: traffic between Patna and the districts of north Bihar funnels onto a small number of bridges, chief among them the Mahatma Gandhi Setu and the JP Setu. The official release said Nitish Setu will ease traffic congestion and strengthen connectivity between north and south Bihar, giving commuters and freight a third major route across the river in the Patna region. For families in Vaishali, Hajipur and the districts beyond, a 20-to-25-minute crossing to the state capital replaces a journey that depended on the load on the older bridges.

The wider package, and a naming row

The bridge was the centerpiece of a ₹34,470 crore day: the projects Modi inaugurated, dedicated or broke ground on span road connectivity, energy, urban infrastructure, water resources, education, healthcare and transport, and the programme included a Griha Pravesh ceremony for more than 26,900 beneficiaries of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban). The bridge's name drew objections from opposition leaders in the days before the inauguration, the Daily Jagran reported, even as the government presented it as recognition of Nitish Kumar's role in the project's development. At the event, Modi also took a swipe at previous governments in Bihar, saying the poor had been looted by earlier administrations.
